text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point and lowers the points of every other member by 0.3. In the same way, every token another member keeps in their own account lowers your points by 0.3.
- Each token in the group account pays you 0.3 points and does not change any other member's points.
- Every round, every member also receives 18 points, whatever anyone does.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
I'm working out the payoff structure of this public goods game: keeping a token yields 1 point to me but costs each of the 3 others 0.3 points, while contributing a token to the group account only pays the contributor 0.3 points and doesn't affect anyone else's payoff.

Comparing social welfare, private tokens net only 0.1 per token for the group as a whole versus 0.3 per token for contributed tokens, meaning full cooperation beats full defection collectively, even though private hoarding is each individual's dominant strategy. Over 10 repeated rounds, I'm thinking through whether opening with full cooperation (contributing all 20 tokens) makes sense as a signal, comparing payoffs if everyone contributes (6 each) versus everyone defects (2 each), and considering how unilateral defection against cooperators would play out.
